newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares firm at open, blue chips up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares firm at open, blue chips up.

text.p: Singapore shares were firmer at the open on Tuesday and dealers said there was some nibbling at selected blue chips by funds in light trading.
"People are not rushing in to buy. But some confidence seems to be returning as Wall Street has kept steady for two days in row," said a broker.
The Straits Times Industrial index rose by 6.98 points to 2,095.12 at 0158 GMT.
Several block trades were crossed early in the morning but activity in the wider market remained muted.
Singapore Telecom saw almost a million shares crossed at prices ranging from S$2.90-S$2.92.

NatSteel also saw a block of 450,000 shares changing hands at S$3.60. "It is seen as a recovery stock after their restructuring. They also have good exposure to the electronics sector," said one broker.
Electronics-based Venture Manufacturing also had a block trade of 836,000 shares crossed at S$3.684.
Early gainers were DBS foreign, Singapore Press foreign, SembCorp and OCBC foreign, all rising 20 cents each. Losers included Cycle & Carriage and Robinson.
